procedure.description: percutaneous transcatheter placement of intracoronary stent, single major coronary artery

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Lanternhill Health Plan denied the claim for CPT 92928 (percutaneous transcatheter placement of intracoronary stent, single major coronary artery) with date of service 2026-01-26. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not establish refractory angina on optimal medical therapy or objective ischemia in the target vessel.

criteria.text: Angina of Canadian Cardiovascular Society class II to IV persisting despite at least two antianginal medications at optimal doses, or documented intolerance.

Objective evidence of ischemia: stress imaging showing a moderate or large reversible defect (10 percent or more of the myocardium), or invasive physiology with fractional flow reserve of 0.80 or less or instantaneous wave-free ratio of 0.89 or less in the target vessel.
Angiographic stenosis of 70 percent or more in the target vessel (50 to 69 percent with abnormal invasive physiology).

chart.text: Mole on the upper back that her spouse noticed. About 6 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Mammogram report forwarded for the record. Bilateral screening, BI-RADS 1, negative, routine screening in one year.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Patient called about a tick bite on the scalp after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 220, LDL 149, HDL 54, triglycerides 135. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.

60 year old woman in cardiology clinic with exertional chest pressure for 7 months, relieved by rest. Hypertension, hyperlipidemia, type 2 diabetes. Stress imaging ordered, medications reviewed and continued. Her history otherwise: anxiety, sees a counselor, seasonal allergies, reflux on omeprazole as needed. Allergies: penicillin, rash. Does not smoke, a glass of wine on weekends, works in an office. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today.
Blood pressure check. 121 over 87 today, 127 over 79 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 20 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
A1c came back 6.0. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 2 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.

Regadenoson SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging. Large reversible perfusion defect of the anterior wall and apex, 12 percent of the left ventricle, with transient ischemic dilation. Ejection fraction 54 percent post-stress.
Metoprolol succinate 100 daily, amlodipine 10 daily, isosorbide mononitrate 60 daily, all at these doses for the past 4 months. Aspirin 81, atorvastatin 80.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 40. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 3.7, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 100. Repeat in a year.

Here with a cough and congestion for 7 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.

Reviewed the stress test. Given the size of the defect and ongoing symptoms on maximal medical therapy, recommended coronary angiography with physiology and intervention if appropriate. Risks reviewed, she agrees. Vitals today 131 over 88, pulse 70. Still class III angina walking one block or climbing a flight despite three antianginal medications at target doses, using nitroglycerin 4 times a week.
Vitamin D came back 16. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
Work note requested for a sick day last Monday. Faxed to the employer.

Coronary angiography. Proximal left anterior descending 82 percent stenosis. Fractional flow reserve across the lesion 0.69. Circumflex and right coronary without significant disease. Proceeded to intervention of the proximal left anterior descending: predilation and a 3.5 by 18 millimeter drug-eluting stent, TIMI 3 flow, no residual stenosis.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
